dimensions.name: Database architecture and migrations
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every table has an explicit primary key and an owner; all schema changes go through versioned, reviewed migrations with tested rollback; production schema is measured equal to the migration history; no schema drift.

checks.title: Every production table has a primary key
checks.acceptance: Read-only catalogue query on production lists tables without a PK; result must be 0 (excluding documented framework tables).

checks.title: Schema changes only through versioned migrations
checks.acceptance: Repository has a migrations directory and a migration ledger table; production ledger head equals the latest migration in the released commit.

checks.title: Migration rehearsal before release
checks.acceptance: Each release with a migration has a recorded rehearsal on a production copy (row counts before/after, no data loss) and a tested rollback script.

checks.title: No schema drift between code and production
checks.acceptance: Generated schema from code compared with production catalogue (read-only); differences = 0 or documented.

dimensions.name: Data integrity and concurrency
dimensions.definitionOf10: All required relationships are enforced and validated foreign keys with zero orphans; NOT NULL/UNIQUE/CHECK constraints encode business rules; concurrent writes are transactional and idempotent; measured on production.

checks.title: Required foreign keys enforced
checks.acceptance: Required-FK coverage (validated required FKs / confirmed required links) measured read-only on production = 100%.

checks.title: Zero orphan rows on required links
checks.acceptance: Orphan query per required link on production returns 0 rows.

checks.title: Business rules as database constraints
checks.acceptance: Critical invariants (amounts >= 0, valid states, unique identities) exist as CHECK/UNIQUE constraints; negative test inserts are rejected in a test database.
references: OWASP ASVS 5.0 Validation and Business Logic

checks.title: Concurrent and repeated writes are safe
checks.acceptance: Integration test runs the same write twice and in parallel; result is one correct record (idempotency key or transaction), no lost update.

dimensions.name: Data quality and provenance
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every critical dataset has measured quality rules (completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency), each record's source and load time are recorded, test data never sits in production, and duplicates are resolved by rule.

checks.title: Quality rules measured on critical datasets
checks.acceptance: Data-quality run on production datasets with a recorded score and failing-rule list, not older than its cadence.

checks.title: Source and load time recorded per record
checks.acceptance: Critical tables carry source system + loaded/updated timestamps; query shows < 1% nulls.

checks.title: No test or fixture data in production
checks.acceptance: Read-only scan for fixture schemas, test emails, seed markers in production = 0 findings.

checks.title: Duplicate identities detected and resolved
checks.acceptance: Duplicate-key queries (email, external id, code) on production = 0 unresolved duplicates.

dimensions.name: Data flows and freshness
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every inbound and outbound flow has an owner, a freshness SLO and monitoring; each flow's last success is measured inside its SLO; failures alert and are reconciled.

checks.title: Each consumed flow has a freshness SLO and owner
checks.acceptance: Flow inventory (eees/flows.json) lists owner, frequency and freshness SLO for every flow the app consumes.

checks.title: Last successful run inside SLO
checks.acceptance: Measured last-success timestamp of every consumed flow is within its SLO on production.

checks.title: Flow failure raises an alert
checks.acceptance: A forced failure in a non-production run produces an alert to the owner within one cycle.

dimensions.name: Integration and API contracts
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every API and integration has a versioned schema, contract tests on both sides, authenticated access, error/retry semantics and an inventory with no undocumented endpoints.

checks.title: API inventory is complete
checks.acceptance: Route inventory generated from code equals documented inventory; undocumented routes = 0.

checks.title: Contract tests for each integration
checks.acceptance: Producer and consumer contract tests exist and pass in CI for every cross-app interface.

checks.title: Inputs validated against a schema
checks.acceptance: Every write endpoint validates its body with a schema; fuzz/negative tests are rejected with 4xx.
references: OWASP ASVS 5.0 Validation and Business Logic

checks.title: Flow documentation complete
checks.acceptance: Every flow the app produces or consumes has every required EEES flow field filled (eees/flows.json requiredFields: the 15 items of the standard, with frequency and freshness SLO and producer and consumer listed separately).

dimensions.name: Cross-application consistency
dimensions.definitionOf10: Each shared entity has one source of truth; copies are reconciled automatically with zero unexplained differences; identities map by stable ids, never by names.

checks.title: Source of truth defined for shared entities
checks.acceptance: Source-of-truth matrix lists the owner for every entity the app shares.

checks.title: Automated reconciliation with zero unexplained differences
checks.acceptance: Reconciliation job compares owner and copy; latest run shows 0 unexplained differences.

checks.title: Records linked by stable ids
checks.acceptance: Cross-app references use ids/external keys; name-based matching = 0 in code review.

dimensions.name: Identity and authentication
dimensions.definitionOf10: All non-public access requires strong authentication (SSO or MFA for humans, scoped tokens for services); sessions expire and are revocable; brute force is limited; verified by negative tests on production.

checks.title: Every non-public route requires authentication
checks.acceptance: Unauthenticated request to every non-public route returns 401/403 (route inventory test).

checks.title: Strong authentication for humans
checks.acceptance: Human sign-in uses SSO or MFA; shared passwords = 0.

checks.title: Sessions expire and failed logins are limited
checks.acceptance: Session lifetime and lockout/rate-limit verified by test.

checks.title: Service-to-service calls use scoped credentials
checks.acceptance: Each integration uses its own token/signature with least scope; reuse of one secret for two purposes = 0.

dimensions.name: Authorization and data isolation
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every object and function access is authorized server-side; users and clients see only their own data; database roles are least-privilege; verified by negative tests and production role inspection.

checks.title: Object-level authorization tested
checks.acceptance: For each object route, a request for another owner's id is refused (negative test suite).

checks.title: Function-level authorization tested
checks.acceptance: Admin/privileged functions refuse ordinary users (negative tests).

checks.title: Database roles are least-privilege
checks.acceptance: Production role inspection: app roles have no SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE or BYPASSRLS; read-only roles cannot write.

checks.title: No cross-client data exposure
checks.acceptance: Data isolation test with two clients shows no leakage across screens, exports and APIs.

dimensions.name: Secrets, encryption and key management
dimensions.definitionOf10: No secret in code or logs; secrets live in a secret store with rotation and owners; data is encrypted in transit and at rest; keys are separated by purpose.

checks.title: No secrets in the repository
checks.acceptance: Secret scan of the full repository and history finds 0 live secrets.

checks.title: No secret files committed
checks.acceptance: No .env or key files tracked in git; an example env file documents names only.

checks.title: Encryption in transit and at rest
checks.acceptance: All endpoints serve HTTPS with HSTS; database storage encryption confirmed by provider settings.

checks.title: Secrets have owners and rotation dates
checks.acceptance: Secret register lists owner, purpose and last rotation for every production secret; none older than policy.

dimensions.name: Application, API and infrastructure security
dimensions.definitionOf10: No known exploitable vulnerability; security headers, input handling and rate limits are verified; infrastructure is hardened; passive and authorized active scans are clean and repeated.

checks.title: Passive security scan clean
checks.acceptance: Latest Secval passive scan of the production host shows 0 high findings.

checks.title: Security headers and TLS configured
checks.acceptance: Response headers include CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection; TLS grade checked.

checks.title: Rate limits on public and API endpoints
checks.acceptance: Burst test in a non-production environment receives 429 after the documented limit.

checks.title: No server-side request forgery or injection paths
checks.acceptance: Static review and tests for SSRF/SQL injection on all routes that take URLs or query input.

dimensions.name: Privacy and data lifecycle
dimensions.definitionOf10: Personal data is inventoried, minimized, retained only as long as documented and deleted on schedule; personal data never appears in code, logs or test fixtures.

checks.title: Personal data inventory
checks.acceptance: Register lists every table/field holding personal data with purpose and legal basis.

checks.title: Retention and deletion enforced
checks.acceptance: Retention job exists; query shows no personal data older than the retention period.

checks.title: No personal data in code, logs or fixtures
checks.acceptance: Scan of repository and sampled logs finds 0 real personal records.

dimensions.name: Audit trails, approvals and governance
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every consequential action is logged append-only with who/what/when; production changes need recorded approval for the exact SHA; logs are tamper-evident and reviewed.

checks.title: Append-only audit trail for consequential actions
checks.acceptance: Audit table cannot be updated/deleted by the app role; write test confirms.
references: OWASP ASVS 5.0 Security Logging and Error Handling

checks.title: Exact-SHA approval before every production deploy
checks.acceptance: Every production deploy in the period maps to a recorded approval of that exact SHA; unapproved deploys = 0.

checks.title: Owner-approved overrides are logged
checks.acceptance: Business overrides (e.g. below-cost price) record approver, reason and time.

dimensions.name: Functional completeness and correctness
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every documented requirement has an acceptance test that passes against production-like data; core user journeys are verified end to end on production.

checks.title: Requirements register with acceptance tests
checks.acceptance: Each user requirement has an id and at least one acceptance test; uncovered requirements = 0.

checks.title: Core journeys pass end to end
checks.acceptance: Browser end-to-end run of every core journey on a production-like copy passes.

checks.title: Core journeys verified on production
checks.acceptance: Read-only production smoke of core journeys after each release passes.

dimensions.name: Business processes and workflow orchestration
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every multi-step business process runs to completion or fails visibly; hand-offs between people, apps and jobs are tracked; no silent stalls.

checks.title: Process steps tracked with state
checks.acceptance: Each workflow instance has a recorded state and owner; stalled instances older than SLA = 0.

checks.title: Failure of a step is visible
checks.acceptance: Forced failure in a test run surfaces to the owner (alert or task).

checks.title: End-to-end process test
checks.acceptance: Integration test executes the whole process with realistic data.

dimensions.name: Protocols, rules and state transitions
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every entity's allowed states and transitions are defined and enforced server-side; illegal transitions are rejected; rule changes are versioned.

checks.title: State machine defined
checks.acceptance: Allowed states and transitions documented for each stateful entity.

checks.title: Illegal transitions rejected server-side
checks.acceptance: Negative tests for illegal transitions return errors and change nothing.
references: OWASP ASVS 5.0 Validation and Business Logic

checks.title: Production data respects the rules
checks.acceptance: Read-only query finds 0 records in impossible states.

dimensions.name: Financial and domain-specific correctness
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every financial and domain figure reconciles to its source of record within tolerance on production; currencies are never mixed; formulas are tested against independent calculations.

checks.title: Figures reconcile to the source of record
checks.acceptance: Reconciliation of key figures (revenue, receivables, prices, positions) to source on production: unexplained difference = 0.

checks.title: Currencies never mixed
checks.acceptance: Every sum is per currency or converted with a dated rate; query/tests show no mixed-currency totals.

checks.title: Formulas verified by independent calculation
checks.acceptance: Golden-case tests computed independently (spreadsheet or second implementation) match the app.

checks.title: Domain invariants hold in production
checks.acceptance: Read-only invariant queries (e.g. price >= cost floor unless approved) return 0 violations.

dimensions.name: AI quality, grounding and agent safety
dimensions.definitionOf10: AI answers are grounded in authorized sources with provenance, measured against an independent benchmark, refuse when unsure, cannot take unapproved actions and resist prompt injection.

checks.title: Factual accuracy on an independent benchmark
checks.acceptance: Blind question set with independent answers; accuracy measured and >= agreed target.

checks.title: Answers cite authorized sources
checks.acceptance: Sampled answers include provenance; retrieval respects the user's permissions.

checks.title: Prompt-injection and excessive-agency tests
checks.acceptance: Injection test set cannot trigger writes, data exfiltration or prompt leakage.

checks.title: Safe fallback when AI is unavailable
checks.acceptance: With the model unavailable or out of quota, the app degrades to a clear message, never a fabricated answer.

dimensions.name: UX, accessibility and usability
dimensions.definitionOf10: Core screens pass WCAG 2.2 AA automated and manual checks on desktop and mobile, show loading/error states, and have no misleading indicators.

checks.title: Automated accessibility check passes
checks.acceptance: axe-core (WCAG 2.x A/AA rules) on every core screen, light and dark: 0 violations.

checks.title: Mobile and desktop layouts work
checks.acceptance: Core screens at 1440/390/360 px: no sideways scroll, controls reachable.

checks.title: Loading, empty and error states shown
checks.acceptance: Browser test forces slow/empty/failed responses; each screen shows a clear state.

dimensions.name: Availability and service-level objectives
dimensions.definitionOf10: Availability SLIs are measured externally, SLOs and error budgets are defined, and production meets them over a sustained window.

checks.title: External uptime measured
checks.acceptance: Independent monitor (Secval uptime) checks the production health endpoint at least every 30 minutes.

checks.title: SLO defined and met over 30 days
checks.acceptance: Documented availability SLO; measured 30-day availability >= SLO.

checks.title: Production version is verifiable
checks.acceptance: A version endpoint returns the exact deployed commit SHA.

dimensions.name: Performance, scalability and capacity
dimensions.definitionOf10: Latency and throughput SLOs are defined and measured on production; capacity limits (DB, storage, quotas) are forecast with alerts before exhaustion.

checks.title: Latency measured against an SLO
checks.acceptance: p95 latency of core endpoints measured on production within its SLO.

checks.title: Capacity forecast with alerts
checks.acceptance: Storage, database and quota usage forecast; alert before 80%.

checks.title: Load behaviour tested off production
checks.acceptance: Load test on a non-production copy at expected peak x2 passes (no live load tests without authorization).

dimensions.name: Resilience and graceful degradation
dimensions.definitionOf10: Dependency failures (database, external APIs, AI) degrade gracefully with timeouts, retries and clear messages; the app restarts cleanly and never crashes on one bad request.

checks.title: Timeouts and retries on every external call
checks.acceptance: Code review/tests: every outbound call has a timeout and bounded retry.

checks.title: Dependency outage drill
checks.acceptance: Simulated database/API outage in a test environment: app stays up and shows a clear message.

checks.title: One bad request cannot crash the server
checks.acceptance: Malformed input tests return 4xx/500 JSON without process exit.
references: OWASP ASVS 5.0 Security Logging and Error Handling

dimensions.name: Observability, monitoring and alerts
dimensions.definitionOf10: Structured logs, metrics and traces cover every critical path; alerts reach an owner with runbooks; alert noise is controlled.

checks.title: Structured logs for critical paths
checks.acceptance: Logs include request id, outcome and no secrets/personal data.
references: OWASP ASVS 5.0 Security Logging and Error Handling

checks.title: Error rate monitored with alert
checks.acceptance: Production error rate measured; alert configured and tested.

checks.title: Alerts reach an owner with a runbook
checks.acceptance: Each alert has an owner and runbook; test alert delivered.

dimensions.name: Backups, disaster recovery and recoverability
dimensions.definitionOf10: Backups of every critical store run on schedule, are kept off-site, and are restored and verified regularly within the documented RPO/RTO; recovery has been proven on production-equivalent data.

checks.title: Backup freshness inside RPO
checks.acceptance: Latest backup of every critical store is younger than its RPO (measured).

checks.title: Off-site copy exists
checks.acceptance: Backup exists in a second provider/account; listing verified.

checks.title: Restore drill passes
checks.acceptance: Restore of the latest backup into an isolated database; row counts and checksums match; RTO measured.

checks.title: Point-in-time recovery window documented
checks.acceptance: Provider PITR window and snapshot schedule documented and checked.

dimensions.name: Background jobs and operational automation
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every scheduled job has an owner, a recorded last success, alerting on failure and idempotent re-runs; no job silently stops.

checks.title: Job register with last success
checks.acceptance: Every scheduled job lists owner, schedule and last success; measured last success inside schedule.

checks.title: Failed jobs alert
checks.acceptance: Forced job failure raises an alert.

checks.title: Re-runs are idempotent
checks.acceptance: Test runs each job twice; no duplicate effect.

dimensions.name: Architecture, code quality and maintainability
dimensions.definitionOf10: Code passes type checks and lint with zero warnings; modules have clear boundaries; duplicated logic is shared; complexity hot spots are tracked.

checks.title: Type check passes
checks.acceptance: Type checker (e.g. tsc --noEmit) exits 0 on the released commit.

checks.title: Lint passes with zero warnings
checks.acceptance: Linter exits 0 with zero warnings.

checks.title: No duplicated business logic
checks.acceptance: Review finds shared formulas in one module (e.g. one FX/currency module).

dimensions.name: Automated testing and independent QA
dimensions.definitionOf10: Automated unit, integration and browser tests cover every critical path and run on every change; an independent reviewer verifies each release; no test is skipped to get green.

checks.title: Test suite present and green
checks.acceptance: Test command exists and passes on the released commit (CI run link).

checks.title: No skipped or quarantined tests
checks.acceptance: Count of skipped/only/quarantined tests = 0 or each documented.

checks.title: Independent QA per release
checks.acceptance: A reviewer other than the implementing agent records a verdict on the exact release SHA.

dimensions.name: CI/CD, deployment and release safety
dimensions.definitionOf10: Every change is built and tested in CI before deploy; deploys happen only from approved, gated commits; rollback is scripted and tested; DORA metrics are measured.

checks.title: CI runs tests on pull requests
checks.acceptance: A CI workflow runs on pull_request and executes the test command.

checks.title: CI cancels superseded runs
checks.acceptance: Every workflow has a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress (cost and correctness).

checks.title: Main branch CI is green
checks.acceptance: Latest finished run on the deploy branch succeeded.

checks.title: Rollback tested
checks.acceptance: Rollback to the previous release performed in a test environment and timed.

dimensions.name: Configuration and environment consistency
dimensions.definitionOf10: Configuration is declared in code (infrastructure as code), environments match, required settings are validated at start-up, and drift is detected.

checks.title: Deployment configuration in the repository
checks.acceptance: Infrastructure/deploy file (render.yaml, fly.toml, Dockerfile) is versioned.

checks.title: Required settings validated at start-up
checks.acceptance: Missing required setting makes start-up fail or a health flag turn red (test).

checks.title: Production settings match the declared configuration
checks.acceptance: Read-only comparison of provider settings with the repository file: differences = 0.

dimensions.name: Dependencies and software supply chain
dimensions.definitionOf10: Dependencies are pinned by lockfile, scanned for known vulnerabilities, updated on a schedule, and CI actions are pinned.

checks.title: Lockfile committed
checks.acceptance: Package lockfile tracked in git.

checks.title: No known high/critical vulnerabilities
checks.acceptance: Dependency audit (npm audit / pip-audit) reports 0 high or critical.

checks.title: Automated dependency updates
checks.acceptance: Dependabot/Renovate (or documented schedule) configured.

dimensions.name: Documentation, ownership and operational readiness
dimensions.definitionOf10: README, ownership, runbooks and release/rollback procedures exist and are current; a new engineer can operate the app from the docs alone.

checks.title: README and ownership documented
checks.acceptance: README plus an ownership/rules file (CLAUDE.md, CODEOWNERS or AGENTS.md) exist.

checks.title: Runbooks for incidents and rollback
checks.acceptance: Runbook covers deploy, rollback, restore and on-call steps; last reviewed within 90 days.

checks.title: Engineering register current
checks.acceptance: Backlog/status/handoff (e.g. .engineering/) updated within the last 7 days.

evidenceLevels.meaning: Synthetic tests or repository inspection only
Production-like end-to-end tests without production verification
Independently verified, sustained over time and operationally proven

scoreBands.meaning: No implementation or no reliable evidence
Development functionality verified mainly through synthetic tests
Realistic end-to-end validation, negative testing and documented risks
Independently verified, sustained, fully controlled and operationally proven

hardGates.text: Confirmed exploitable critical security flaw, unauthorized client-data access or active exposed credential
Critical data corruption, incorrect financial posting or failed recovery of critical data
No sustained production monitoring or independent final QA

tiers.meaning: Financial or sensitive client/personal data; strongest proof required
